explanation: In Indonesian business and social settings, brief or intermittent eye contact is generally preferred over sustained staring, especially with elders or superiors, where prolonged eye contact can come across as confrontational. Glancing down occasionally while listening is read as humility and respect rather than disinterest. Casual eye contact among peers is generally unremarkable.
local_tip: With elders or senior colleagues, hold eye contact in short stretches and look away occasionally rather than maintaining a constant, steady gaze.

also_check.note: Prolonged eye contact can read as confrontational; brief glances are more comfortable.
Steady eye contact is read as a sign of confidence and honesty.
Eye contact between men is normal, but between genders it is usually kept brief and minimal.

sources.title: How To Follow Business Etiquette in Indonesia
